For a single‑owner personal loan, the most likely situations and next steps are:

1. Loan is tied to a different online profile  
   - If you’ve ever:
     - Changed your email or phone and created a new login, or  
     - Had an older online banking username  
   then the loan might still be linked to that old profile.  
   → Try signing out and logging in with any older username you remember, or use “Forgot username” with your old email/phone if that’s an option.

2. Loan exists on your customer record but isn’t linked to online banking  
   This can happen if:
   - The loan was opened in branch/over phone long ago, and online access was never set up or got disconnected.  
   → In this case, only bank staff can relink it.

To get your current balance and fix access, contact the bank (phone or branch) and say something like:

“I have a personal loan only in my name that I’ve had for several years. It’s with your bank, but when I log in, I don’t see any accounts at all. Can you verify my identity, locate the loan, tell me the current balance, and link this loan to my current online banking profile?”

They may ask for:
- Your full name and DOB  
- The last 4 of your SSN (or equivalent ID)  
- The approximate original loan amount and when you opened it

Once they link it correctly, you should then be able to ask me again here and I’ll be able to pull the balance directly.

Do you have access to the bank’s customer service number or nearby branch to make that call/visit today?</action>
